title: RMIT Emergency and crisis support
content: For urgent mental health support, RMIT provides a 24/7 urgent support phone and text service. In Australia, call 000 when there is immediate danger. This service is for urgent or crisis situations rather than routine counselling.

title: RMIT Counselling and Psychological Services
content: RMIT Counselling and Psychological Services provides free, confidential, professional short-term counselling for students experiencing concerns such as stress, anxiety or low mood. Students can seek support even when the situation is not a crisis. The service can also refer students to other suitable supports.

title: RMIT Safer Community
content: Safer Community is a free and confidential RMIT service for students and staff seeking support about violence, sexual harm, concerning, unwanted, uncomfortable or threatening behaviour. It can provide advice, support and referral, but it is not an emergency service.

title: RMIT Student Welfare Advisors
content: Student Welfare Advisors provide free and confidential short-term assistance to students who are struggling to navigate university processes and support. They can assist with finance, accommodation, complex or urgent support needs, and referrals to other services.

title: RMIT Student Hardship Assistance Grants
content: Student Hardship Assistance Grants provide short-term one-off assistance for students experiencing financial hardship. Support may help with urgent essential needs such as food, travel, living expenses, medical costs and direct study expenses.

title: RMIT Financial welfare advice
content: Students experiencing financial difficulty can speak with a Welfare Advisor about financial assistance, emergency accommodation, budgeting and available support options, including hardship assistance and emergency vouchers.

title: RMIT Equitable Learning and disability support
content: Equitable Learning Services supports students with a disability, neurodivergence, long-term illness or mental health condition. The team can work with eligible students to create an Equitable Learning Plan and arrange ongoing study support and adjustments.
